prose: |
  Wiring (beadle-aw4):

  NewMailHandler now takes a *PipelineStore parameter, stores it on
  MailHandler, and OnNewMail's Executor construction sets Store: h.store.
  main.go passes the same PipelineStore instance it already builds for the
  startup sweep -- no second store is constructed, so both halves agree on
  the pipelines directory. Executor.save()'s nil-Store guard is untouched;
  pipeline.go and pipeline_test.go were not modified at all (outside the
  write set, and the guard was already correct -- the defect was only that
  production never set the field).

  Verification that this actually closes the gap, not just that save() is
  called: TestExecutor_Run_PersistsToDisk in persist_test.go runs an
  Executor with a real PipelineStore through Run() end to end and reads the
  resulting record back off disk with os.ReadFile + json.Unmarshal,
  asserting on the on-disk content (status, ID, email, results) -- not on a
  mock recording a Save call.

  Startup sweep (LoadRunning -> mark failed -> Save) is extracted from
  runCmd.RunE into sweepStalePipelines(store, logger) so it is directly
  testable. TestSweepStalePipelines_MarksRunningAsFailed writes a "running"
  record with PipelineStore.Save, calls sweepStalePipelines, and reads the
  file back off disk to confirm it was relabeled "failed" with the exact
  reason string "daemon stopped while pipeline was running". This is the
  first time that path has been exercisable end to end -- before the
  wiring fix nothing ever wrote a record for it to find, so the block was
  unreachable in practice, exactly as beadle-aw4 described.
  TestSweepStalePipelines_CompletedRecordUntouched and
  TestSweepStalePipelines_EmptyDirIsNoop cover the two paths that must NOT
  relabel anything.

  The TRUST BOUNDARY contract on LoadRunning is unchanged and honored:
  sweepStalePipelines does nothing with a loaded Pipeline except overwrite
  Status/Error and Save it back. No field of the loaded struct drives any
  execution decision. I did not touch LoadRunning's implementation or its
  doc comment.

  Retention (my call per the contract's "you own the decision" instruction):

  Implemented PipelineStore.Prune(maxAge time.Duration) (int, error) in
  persist.go, called from main.go once at startup, immediately after
  sweepStalePipelines and before the poller starts. Policy: age-based on
  Pipeline.CreatedAt (no schema change -- CreatedAt already exists), default
  30 days via a new DefaultRetention constant. A "running" record is never
  removed regardless of age, on the same principle as the TRUST BOUNDARY
  comment above -- Prune must not destroy the only record of a pipeline
  that might still be executing; if a crash left one stale, the sweep marks
  it failed first (now eligible), which is why Prune runs strictly after
  the sweep in main.go, not before or interleaved. Unreadable/corrupt files
  are logged and skipped, matching LoadRunning's existing posture, rather
  than treated as errors that abort the whole prune pass.

  Why 30 days and why age-based rather than count-based or size-based: each
  record holds email metadata (from, subject, message_id) plus every
  stage's raw output, so this is a data-retention question, not just a
  disk-space one -- a count or size cap would keep old, potentially
  sensitive content around indefinitely as long as volume stays low, which
  doesn't match the "records no longer accumulate without bound" framing
  in the contract as well as a fixed calendar window does. 30 days is long
  enough to debug a failure discovered days after the fact (the daemon's
  own log file is not rotated either, so pipeline records are currently the
  more structured of the two artifacts for postmortems) and short enough
  that a long-lived daemon doesn't accumulate an unbounded audit trail.
  This is a judgment call, not a design fork: nothing about it changes an
  existing contract, only adds a new one, so I implemented it rather than
  escalating, per the contract's instruction to escalate only a genuine
  fork.

  I considered making Prune run per-message instead of once at startup
  (e.g. sweep after every pipeline completes) but rejected it: pruning is
  cheap relative to mailbox polling cadence, gains nothing from running
  more often than once per process lifetime, and a startup-only sweep
  keeps the hot path (OnNewMail) free of directory-scan I/O.

  Everything else: Pipeline's schema and Status semantics are unchanged (I
  did not add fields or touch pipeline.go); Error may still be non-empty on
  a "completed" pipeline, which Prune does not care about since it prunes
  by CreatedAt/Status only. Three commits, one per logical step (wiring,
  retention primitive + persistence test, startup integration + sweep
  test), each green on make check before the next started.
